Fabless: The Transformation of the Semiconductor Industry and How I Wrote the Book

7 Jun 2022 • 2 minute read

...

If you are attending, I will be there giving away copies of Cadence's latest book, which I wrote along with Frank Schirrmeister, with editing by Tanushri Shah.

...

But I also want to plug another book that Daniel Nenni and I wrote several years ago, with a foreword by TSMC's Cliff Hou. Since it is mostly a history of how semiconductors went from the era where every semiconductor company had its own fabs to an era where very few of them did, it is not something that goes out of date. If anything, the message of the book has only got stronger now that there are just three foundries that can build chips that require EUV lithography (plus some dedicated memory fabs). Dan and I revised the book in 2019 to produce a second edition, with a completely new last chapter of predictions (largely written by Wally Rhines).
That book is Fabless: The Transformation of the Semiconductor Industry . If you absolutely have to have a hard copy, then it is available on Amazon for $15. But the SemiWiki book page has a free download.

Fabless

by Daniel Nenni and Paul McLellan · 2013
The industry-insider account of how splitting chip design from chip manufacturing remade semiconductors -- and made Moore's Law survivable.
Worth reading? Fabless explains a decision that reshaped the entire chip industry: separating the company that designs a chip from the company that manufactures it. Compared to Chip War's sweeping geopolitical narrative, this is a narrower, more technical business history, written by two longtime industry insiders (one of them ran SemiWiki) rather than journalists. It reads more like an industry trade report than a mass-market narrative, and several chapters are contributed by executives from companies telling their own corporate history, so expect

...

ominant model and how TSMC's foundry business grew out of that split. Skip it if you want a current picture of the industry -- treat this as history, not a 2026 snapshot.
